references.text: Pilate had already met with Jesus' accusers when they brought him before him. Here in Luke 23:1 we see the beginning of the trial where the chief priests, the council members, and the people brought Jesus to Pilate.
Pilate had already declared that he found no guilt in Jesus (Luke 23:4–5), and now he summoned the accusers again to announce his decision after the hearing before Herod.
The chief priests and council members whom Pilate summoned were the same leaders who had interrogated Jesus before the Sanhedrin, as described in Luke 22:66.

Pilate had sent Jesus to Herod (Luke 23:8–11), and after Herod also found nothing worthy of punishment in him, he sent Jesus back. Verse 13 marks the moment when Pilate gathers all parties after Herod's hearing.
Also in John 18:38, Pilate declares that he finds no guilt in Jesus and goes out to the Jews to announce this – a parallel to his gathering of the chief priests, council members, and people here.

In John 19:4–6, Pilate brings Jesus out to the chief priests and servants and again declares that he finds no guilt in him. This is a parallel to Pilate's gathering of the leaders and the people in Luke 23:13.
In Matthew 27:17, Pilate gathers the crowd to ask whom they want released. This shows the same pattern where Pilate addresses both the leaders and the assembled crowd.

In Mark 15:1, it is described that the chief priests, the elders, the scribes, and the whole council held a consultation and handed Jesus over to Pilate – the same groups that Pilate now summons in Luke 23:13.

Peter later refers to this event in Acts 3:13–14, where he says that the people denied Jesus before Pilate's face, even though Pilate had decided to release him. This confirms the role of the chief priests, council members, and the people in condemning Jesus.

In Acts 4:27 it is mentioned that Herod and Pontius Pilate, together with the Gentile nations and the tribes of Israel, gathered against Jesus – a summary that reflects the actors Pilate summoned in Luke 23:13.
